column2: Artifact signature and attestation verification: the producer supply-chain-policy.md consumes (its Q6 was adopted as "a separate sibling spec"). Must cover each ecosystem mechanism the format specs raise: Cosign signatures and attestations via OCI referrers, npm provenance and registry signatures, PEP 740 attestations and Trusted Publishing, Galaxy collection signatures, Maven .asc sidecars, NuGet author and repository signatures, Terraform provider GPG signatures, Hex and Alpine repository keys. Trust roots, key distribution, Sigstore/Rekor transparency, what "verified" means as a stored fact, whether verification is at ingest, at resolution, or both, and how a verdict is exposed to policy. Read supply-chain-policy.md, pypi.md, ansible-collections.md and the other format specs' signing sections first.

The shared signing and generated-index service: the thing write-triggered-services-prototype.md prototypes and that Debian, RPM, Alpine, Arch, Hex, Hackage (TUF), Helm index.yaml, Maven metadata, Cargo index files, conda repodata and CRAN PACKAGES all need. Key custody (the handler must never hold signing material), per-repository vs instance keys, rotation, HSM/KMS backing, publishing public keys to clients, regeneration triggering and coalescing under concurrent publishes, one-snapshot-per-publish, and large generated documents as CAS-backed metadata. Read write-triggered-services-prototype.md, data-model.md, storage-and-gc.md, and every format spec that has a generated or signed index.

The registry-owned management surface: the shared home that pypi.md, npm.md, ansible-collections.md (and Helm, Composer, conda, CRAN, CPAN, Cargo, RubyGems) now cite for operations no or few ecosystem clients perform: yank and unyank, deprecate, delete, retire, filename retirement, and repository-level administration. Read docs/internal/analysis/management-surfaces-and-the-oracle.md first: the trigger is verified by our integration tests and the effect by real clients. Decide one API shape (resource model, versioning, auth scopes it needs from auth.md, audit events it emits), how every management write is a deletion path storage-and-gc.md knows about and a snapshot-creating write in data-model.md's sense, and a CLI or API-first stance.

Asynchronous operations as a shared concept: Galaxy imports return a task id to poll, and other formats have similar shapes (conda and NuGet indexing delays, Maven Central-style staging, security scans in supply-chain-policy.md, replication transfers). The shared data model had no entity for an asynchronous operation (ansible-collections.md Q1, write-triggered-services-prototype.md Q1). Define the entity or entities, their lifecycle, polling and completion semantics, failure and retry, visibility in the API, and how an operation's completion relates to the one-snapshot-per-publish rule. Coordinate with data-model.md, which owns entities: whatever you define must be expressible there, and list the exact data-model.md amendment as a sibling consequence.

Upstream adapters as a separate axis from format handlers: Harbor's lesson that one OCI handler needs many upstream adapters (Docker Hub, ECR, GCR, GHCR, Quay, Artifactory, Nexus) because they differ in auth and quirks, not wire format; and format-handler-interface.md's own note that no spec owns the adapter interface's shape. Define the adapter interface, how an Upstream row selects an adapter, credential types (static token, OAuth dance, cloud IAM such as ECR's GetAuthorizationToken and GCR's metadata-server tokens), rate-limit handling (Docker Hub pull limits), and conformance testing against real upstreams on the nightly job proxy-cache.md defines.

Observability: metrics, logs and traces for a registry. proxy-cache.md requires quota utilisation and cache-thrash detection to be observable, storage-and-gc.md needs GC progress and pinned-storage reporting, supply-chain-policy.md needs refusal records, replication.md needs lag. Define the metric set (with names and labels), structured logging with credential redaction (auth.md's credential-leak criteria), OpenTelemetry tracing across handler, Deps and storage, health and readiness endpoints, and an audit log of security-relevant events distinct from operational logs.

Deployment, configuration and operations: single binary vs components, configuration surface (file, env, flags; the vendored cobra-viper skill is binding for the CLI and config), PostgreSQL and object-storage requirements, Helm chart and container image, TLS termination (auth.md requires TLS for credentials), horizontal scaling and which components must be singletons (storage-and-gc.md's single deleter), leader election, backup and restore of PostgreSQL plus the CAS, upgrade and migration policy, and resource sizing. Read storage-and-gc.md, auth.md, replication.md and the charter.

The web UI: project-charter.md Q6 is being adopted as "the charter gains a web UI criterion and a sibling spec", and the prior-art survey names Pulp's weak UI as a reason the field is open. TypeScript frontend (the charter's language section). Browse and search across all formats, per-format install snippets, repository and upstream administration, token management (oci.md's token-management surface question), policy refusals and audit views, and GC/pinned-storage visibility. Every UI action must go through the same API as automation (no UI-only capability). Accessibility and a real-browser test strategy, since no real package client exercises a UI.

Repository lifecycle: creation, configuration, renaming, archival and deletion of local, remote and virtual repositories. The storage-and-gc.md gate review recorded that repository deletion exists in no spec at all. Define what deleting a repository does to its pointers (storage-and-gc's fifth mark root), snapshots, cached content, replication links, tokens and policies; whether deletion is soft first; how virtual repository membership reacts when a member is deleted; and every deletion path's relationship to the deletion-intent barrier.

The credential-management surface: registry token issue, list, rotate and revoke, plus the expiry-warning criterion auth.md promised. auth.md resolved Q15 says oci.md Q3 decision creates this spec, and it is on OCI Phase 1 critical path (docker login presents a registry token as the Basic password; the token endpoint issues no refresh token). Also define the credential kind that can hold grants on more than one repository, because oci.md AC1 needs one credential with grants on two repositories for the official conformance suite while auth.md adopted single-repository tokens: reconcile that here and state the exact auth.md amendment as a sibling consequence. Machine vs human credentials, service principals for CI, token display-once semantics, hashing per auth.md, audit events, and the UI and CLI surfaces that call it.
